title: LPTA trace record
description: One line of the JSONL trace emitted by src/LPTAInstrumentation.cpp. Two record shapes share one file, distinguished by record_type: 'pass' (one per pass invocation, the original Phase 1/2 record) and 'analysis' (one per actual analysis (re)computation -- Tier 2 timing experiment, added in 2.1.0). schema_version follows independent SemVer from the tool itself. A new OPTIONAL field, or a new record_type value existing consumers can safely ignore, is a minor bump; a renamed/removed field or a changed meaning for an existing field is a major bump, and both old and new meanings must be documented in RESEARCH.md/CHANGELOG.md for at least one release cycle.

schema_version.description: SemVer of this schema. Records without this field predate versioning (schema_version 1.0.0, retroactively). Records with record_type absent entirely predate the pass/analysis split (schema_version < 2.1.0) and should be treated as record_type='pass'.

record_type.description: 'pass': one pass invocation (Phase 1/2 fields below). 'analysis': one actual analysis (re)computation with CPU timing (Tier 2 fields below).

unit_kind.description: Granularity of the IR unit. 'analysis' records are always 'function' (the four tracked analyses -- DominatorTreeAnalysis, LoopAnalysis, MemorySSAAnalysis, ScalarEvolutionAnalysis -- are all Function-keyed).

unit_name.description: Identifies the IR unit: bare function name for 'function' AND 'loop' kind (see the report layer's report_group_key() for why a viewer needs unit_kind too, not unit_name alone, to distinguish them), '<module:NAME>' for module, '<scc:...>' for SCC, '<unknown>' otherwise.

seq.description: Monotonically increasing per-process sequence number, shared across both record types, assigned at emit time. Use this to order events within one trace file; do not assume it's stable across separate runs/LLVM versions.

pass.description: record_type='pass' only. LLVM pass name as reported by PassInstrumentation, e.g. 'SimplifyCFGPass'.

invalidated.description: record_type='pass' only. True if the pass invalidated its IR unit outright (e.g. deleted a function). When true, none of the after_*/ir_changed/cfg_changed fields are present — the unit could not be safely re-printed.

ir_changed.description: record_type='pass' only. Before/after printed IR text differs. Absent when invalidated=true.

lines_added.description: record_type='pass' only. Line-level LCS diff of printed IR text; 0 when ir_changed=false. Falls back to a multiset approximation for module-scale text (see diffLines()'s size cap in LPTAInstrumentation.cpp) — treat as approximate above roughly 2000x2000 lines.

cfg_changed.description: record_type='pass' only. Proxy signal: true if before/after basic-block count OR total successor-edge count differs. Not exact CFG isomorphism (see ROADMAP.md Phase 1 known limitations).

all_preserved.description: record_type='pass' only. PreservedAnalyses::areAllPreserved() at the end of this pass.

dt_live_before_pass.description: record_type='pass' only. Phase 2: was DominatorTree actually cached (computed and not yet invalidated) for this function immediately before this pass ran. Derived from AfterAnalysisCallback/AnalysisInvalidatedCallback tracking, not from PreservedAnalyses. This is the field that fixes Phase 1's over-firing: 'not preserved' only matters if something was there to preserve.

loop_info_live_before_pass.description: record_type='pass' only. Same as dt_live_before_pass, for LoopAnalysis.

memoryssa_live_before_pass.description: record_type='pass' only (2.1.0+). Same as dt_live_before_pass, for MemorySSAAnalysis -- one of the two 'cascade cost' analyses the Tier 2 experiment is specifically about (see RESEARCH.md/PRODUCTIONIZATION.md experiment notes: MemorySSA/ScalarEvolution are the expensive analyses a bare none() needlessly drags down, not DominatorTree itself).

scev_live_before_pass.description: record_type='pass' only (2.1.0+). Same as dt_live_before_pass, for ScalarEvolutionAnalysis.

dt_wasted_recompute_count.description: record_type='pass' only. Running count (monotonic within this trace) of times DominatorTree has been invalidated for this function AND later actually recomputed (i.e. some later pass asked for it again) — a measured cost, not a suspicion. 0 does not mean invalidation never happened, only that nothing has needed DT again yet.

memoryssa_wasted_recompute_count.description: record_type='pass' only (2.1.0+). Same as dt_wasted_recompute_count, for MemorySSAAnalysis.

scev_wasted_recompute_count.description: record_type='pass' only (2.1.0+). Same as dt_wasted_recompute_count, for ScalarEvolutionAnalysis.

incremental_update_candidate.description: record_type='pass' only. Derived signal (Phase 2, liveness-aware): cfg_changed && dt_live_before_pass && !dt_preserved. Requiring liveness fixes Phase 1's coarser 'cfg_changed && !dt_preserved' (schema_version 1.0.0 records), which over-fired when DominatorTree simply hadn't been computed yet — see RESEARCH.md §5. A true value here now means DominatorTree was demonstrably cached and then discarded by a CFG-changing pass, not merely that it could theoretically have been preserved. Deliberately still DT-specific, not redefined to also cover MemorySSA/ScalarEvolution waste -- those are surfaced via the memoryssa_*/scev_* fields and the 'analysis' record_type instead, to avoid another meaning change to this specific field.

analysis.description: record_type='analysis' only (2.1.0+). Which analysis was (re)computed: one of 'DominatorTreeAnalysis', 'LoopAnalysis', 'MemorySSAAnalysis', 'ScalarEvolutionAnalysis' (the four tracked; see LPTAInstrumentation.cpp's isTrackedAnalysis() -- BranchProbabilityInfo/RegionInfo are real DT dependents too but out of scope for this first timing pass).

cpu_time_us.description: record_type='analysis' only. Process CPU time (user+sys, via llvm::sys::Process::GetTimeUsage -- the same technique LLVM's own -time-passes uses) spent in this specific (re)computation. Deliberately CPU time, not wall-clock: wall-clock on a shared/virtualized machine picks up scheduling noise this metric is built to avoid. On trivially small inputs this can be at or below OS timer-resolution noise -- treat single-digit-microsecond values as approximate; the signal is far more reliable on real, larger programs.

wasted_recompute.description: record_type='analysis' only. True if this specific (re)computation followed an invalidation of this analysis for this function that was never actually needed until now becoming needed again -- i.e. this specific compute's CPU time is the measured cost of Phase 2's dt_wasted_recompute_count (or the memoryssa_/scev_ equivalents) incrementing. Only ever true for a recompute that would not have been necessary had the prior pass preserved this analysis.
